description: Minecraft Mod that brings Functioning Ham Radios into the game - Funded by the ARRL

mods.name: RadioCraft
mods.description:
Radiocraft is a Minecraft mod that adds ham radio (also known as Amateur Radio) into Minecraft Java edition.

* Adds realistic, immersive communication
*Survival-friendly, challenging, and satisfying functionality
* Educational and accurate (albeit simplified) representations of the real ham radio hobby!

What is Ham Radio?

Ham radio is a hobby and service that involves using the radio frequency spectrum for various purposes, such as communication, experimentation, education, and emergency assistance. Ham radio operators, also known as amateur radio operators or hams, need to obtain a license from their government to operate on certain frequency bands and follow certain rules. Ham radio allows hams to talk to other hams across the world, or even into space, using different modes of transmission, such as voice, text, image, and data. Ham radio is also a way to meet new people, learn new skills, and have fun!

releases.notes:
# RadioCraft alpha 1.10.0

Everything since 1.9.2, including 1.9.3's config fix (1.9.3 was never published). Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge. Needs
Simple Voice Chat; [Another Weather Mod](https://github.com/RadiocraftARRL/AnotherWeatherMod) 1.10.0 is optional and
adds live storms, tornado watches and day outlooks to the weather reports and WEFAX charts.

## Changes that affect existing worlds

- **Every telephone needs a Phone PABX now.** A microwave radio is no longer a phone exchange on its own: phones that
  were wired straight to a microwave radio say NO LINE until a powered PABX joins them (see Telephones below).
- **Plain wire only carries power.** Teletypes, faxes, WEFAX receivers, radio interfaces, the tape player, the
  Ionospheric Processor, wired speakers and microwave stations that do not touch their radio now link over the new
  data wire. Rewire them with data wire.

## Telephones

- **Phone PABX**, the exchange every phone needs: phones touching it or on its data wire call each other by
  extension. It needs power (`pabx_power_use`, 2 a tick) and its lamp shows green when it has it.
- Right click a PABX to set its **master number**, its **first extension** (its phones are numbered from it, 100 by
  default) and whether it is **behind another PABX**.
- PABXes on a microwave link (touching a radio, or on its data wire) are dialed by master number then extension: with
  master number 602, extension 100 is `602100`. A PABX behind another works like one of its lines, its number dialed
  before the extension, so you can build a whole phone network.
- The phone shows its full number and who is calling; the call timer now counts (it stuck at 0:00).
- Telephones have their own guide chapter, with a tip on Simple Voice Chat: with push-to-talk, hold its key while you
  speak on a phone; open mic never keys a radio.

## Wiring and antennas

- **Data wire**: a light grey wire for the station's data and audio lines (see above).
- **Antenna switch**: one radio to one of three antennas. Its input turns to the radio's coax by itself; a knob picks
  the output.
- **Receive-only antenna splitter**: every radio behind it hears the antenna, a little weaker; none can transmit
  through it. Recipe: four coax round an iron ingot.
- A radio on a dummy load plays only a faint hiss.

## Weather

- **WEFAX alarms**: the receiver gives a redstone signal, 1 for a message, 2 for a severe thunderstorm, 3 for a
  tornado watch and 4 for a hurricane (the strongest alert wins), and beeps.
- Tornado watches and today's and tomorrow's outlook from Another Weather Mod on the WEFAX and in weather reports.
- Lightning breaks the handhelds and manpacks a struck player carries (`lightning_breaks_carried_radios`), and a
  manpack hurts more (`lightning_manpack_extra_damage`).

## Sound

- Two stations on one frequency now mix: SSB adds them, FM captures the stronger and flips between them when they are
  close. Received levels glide instead of jumping (`voice_level_smoothing`).
- The redstone interference noise no longer goes off near Another Weather Mod's weather instruments in a storm (their
  readings are not switching), follows the radio's volume knob, and fades with distance like the static. The
  teletype and WEFAX chatter fade with distance too.

## Fixes and looks

- `radiocraft-server.toml` no longer corrects itself on every load, and edited band frequencies stay
  ([issue #102](https://github.com/RadiocraftARRL/RadioCraft/issues/102)).
- The radio fax's case uses its wood's planks.
- The HF manpack screen no longer overlaps; its battery reading sits at the right of the window.
- Breaking a WEFAX receiver (or a lit charge controller) shows its own particles, not the missing-texture ones.
- The antenna switch knob no longer flickers.
- Guide builds face their gear toward you, draw their antenna wires, and gain a microwave site.

releases.notes:
# RadioCraft alpha 1.9.2

A fix for 1.9.1, which could not start at all: the game stopped with `Failed to load mod file
META-INF/jarjar/sable-companion-common-1.21.1-1.6.0.jar`. The build step that fixed 1.9.0's JOrbis crash also unpacked
the bundled Sable Companion library, so the jar named a file it no longer had. The library is bundled intact again.
Sable stays optional; RadioCraft starts without it. Every release is now launched on a real NeoForge server and client
before it is published. Nothing else changed.

releases.notes:
# RadioCraft alpha 1.9.1

A fix for 1.9.0, which could not start on a client ([issue #101](https://github.com/hammcmod/RadioCraft/issues/101)):
the game closed at once with `Module neoforge.coremods reads more than one module named jorbis`. The tape decoder's
JOrbis library was packed as a second copy of a module the Minecraft client already ships. It is now shaded into the
mod under its own package, so there is only one. Dedicated servers were not affected. Nothing else changed.

releases.notes:
# RadioCraft alpha 1.9.0

Everything since the 1.2.0 release (commit 1476893, 2026-10-21). Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge. Needs Simple Voice
Chat; [Another Weather Mod](https://github.com/ITCMD/AnotherWeatherMod) 1.9.0 is optional and adds live storms to the
weather reports and WEFAX charts.

## Radios

- Each radio's frequency, mode and S-meter show on its model's screen (hidable in the client config), and the gain
  and mic gain dials work.
- The desk microphone works: hold to talk, sneak-click to lock, quieter with distance, with a timeout. Sneak-right-
  click a radio to take its hand mic on a cord; walk away and it snaps back.
- CW from the keyboard (Left Alt, rebindable) and from Chat Morse.
- Desk speakers, the wall speaker and the loudspeaker play the radio's audio; floor cables are drawn between radios
  and the accessories beside them.
- The HF manpack, worn on the back: a QRP whip, SSB and CW. The VHF handheld goes on the Curios belt with a talk key
  and drains its battery over days.
- FM receivers hiss under a weak signal and are silent otherwise.
- A bad SWR blows a radio's transmitter and poor-crystal radios can explode.
- Callsigns: choose your own real-format ham callsign, or let the game pick one, the first time you reach for a
  radio (`/callsign claim`). Repeaters get X#XX callsigns by distance from spawn. Operator moderation with
  `/radio moderateall` and `/radio moderate <player>`.

## Antennas and matching

- New antennas: delta loop, Moxon, the Hustler 5-BTV multiband vertical, the VHF Ringo, the 2-bay folded dipole
  (found at sites) and the ionosonde antenna.
- The antenna tuner is a real manual tuner with three dials and a tuning lamp. The new automatic tuner tunes itself
  on a band change and gives up with TUNE FAIL past its range.
- The duplexer's six cavity screws tune its TX and RX cavities; a badly tuned duplexer desenses its repeater. Coax
  behind a repeater runs up into its duplexer, and tuners join a radio by touching.
- Lightning: antennas draw strikes, lightning rods work as VHF antennas, and a strike blows the radios on an
  antenna, burns its coax and can light the batteries.
- `/bandcalculate <from> <to>` lists every band between two points, counting terrain losses.

## Propagation and solar weather

- Terrain-aware propagation: hills block line of sight, cliffs cost HF, valley walls cut low-angle skip, handhelds
  are weaker indoors. The terrain map is saved with the world and refreshed as chunks change.
- Sporadic E opens VHF for long range in good conditions, 10m has a long single-hop skip zone, and the aurora can
  appear at any Z.
- Propagation scaling for large servers: receivers out of any possible reach are skipped with one distance check,
  and fixed stations keep their terrain result until a chunk on the path changes.
- The solar weather station became the Teletype Machine: a 400-line roll that prints the solar report and RTTY at
  6 characters a second with real teletype sounds, collisions and per-line moderation. The Ionosonde and the
  Ionospheric Processor measure conditions for it.

## Power

- The large battery takes and gives Forge Energy, so Create water wheels and other mods' generators charge it; with
  Create installed, RadioCraft adds an alternator. Power is balanced around a large water wheel.
- The charge controller switch works; the repeater, the H19 terminal and the automatic tuner draw power.
- Power wire is now thin and comes in sixteen colours; coax is dyeable too. Wire bundles carry up to seven cables
  in one block, keeping their order round bends and up tower legs. The Wire Junction joins power wire of any colour.
- Hazards: a closed loop of power wire shorts and burns through, wet plain wire electrocutes, an open end in the
  rain sparks, and large batteries catch fire from flame, lava, a flint and steel or lightning. Four or more
  burning together explode. Server config `Battery Fires`.

releases.notes:
#### Fixes
- HF Radios work again, like at all (NeoForge broke a lot)
- Antennas can be slightly off and still work, just less well
- Placing a VHF repeater no longer crashes the world
- Wires no longer use 8GB of ram just by existing (100MB now)
- Solar panels next to eachother now connect without a wire
#### New Features
- Reworked the static calculation and implementation
- Added voice effects that sound like radio
- Redstone clocks and circuits can cause RF interference
- Loosely implemented the TNC for APRS, messaging, and file sending (books/maps)
- TXing can cause redstone interference
- Reworked wires so they now hug walls
- Gave coax its own item texture and block texture
- Adjacent frequencies interract with eachother
- Added the Simplex Repeater/Parrot block (great for testing).
- Lightning strikes now cause momentary intererence spikes
- Solar Events were reworked and properly effect radio bands
- Implemented the solar weather station with a text ui for now
- 3 days after a solar blackout, there's a chance of an aurora if above z -1K or below z 2K
- Auroras cause hf interference like solar events do, but cause massive skip for vhf
- Added visible auroras in the sky, and they look damn sexy if I'm being honest.
- No but really they look so good I jumped up and down when I added it in.
- Please comment "Nice aurora @W1btr" in the discord if you like them too.
- Added 4:1 balun for off-center fed antennas (untested)
- Implemented All Band Radio
#### Known Issues
- Static has an audible loop skip. We're looking for someone to fix the ogg file for clean loop.
- S-meters are broken or missing on most radios.
- Many items and blocks are still not implemented
- Duplexer tuning, SWR consequences, Charge Controllers, and some more antenna types are still incomplete
- Recipes are imperfect and missing. Feedback wanted.
